_comment: Mutation testing for packages/core (ADR-001, CORE-04: at least 70%).
Coverage says a line ran. Mutation says that if the line had been wrong, a test would
have noticed — which is the property a port actually needs, because every line here
ran during the differential and that proved nothing on its own.
It runs over the whole suite except test/pipeline-10k.test.ts, which Stryker cannot
execute: instrumented, ten thousand pipeline runs blow past any sane per-test timeout
and the dry run fails outright. Raising the timeout would be worse — a mutant that
merely made the core slower would score as killed-by-timeout, and the number would
start measuring performance. vitest.stryker.config.ts carries that one exclusion.
The differentials ARE included. An earlier version left them out on the theory that a
byte-for-byte oracle comparison kills every mutant and so measures the oracle rather
than the tests — true, and still not a reason to leave real tests out of the package's
own gate. That question is asked separately, without a threshold, by
stryker.units.config.json — see `make mutate-ts-units`.
Not in `make verify`: a full run is tens of minutes against a five-minute budget for
the whole gate. It runs nightly, and `break` makes it fail on its own rather than
through a wrapper that could forget to check.
## `break` is a ratchet (ADR-010)
70 is still the target, and it is still CORE-04b, which blocks CORE-07 — the oracle
cannot retire until this suite is shown to catch regressions without it.
`break` is the LAST MEASURED SCORE, and it may only ever rise. Measured 55.43 on
2026-10-03 over 1869 mutants (809 survived, 24 timed out, 678 tests in the dry run).
This is stricter than it looks, which is the point. A fixed break of 70 against a
score of 55 cannot detect a drop from 55 to 45: it fails identically either way, so
the floor was protecting nothing while appearing to protect everything. At the
measured score the gate finally means 'no change may make this worse'.
Lowering this number is a quality-gate relaxation and a `human-needed` issue with an
ADR, exactly as CLAUDE.md says. Raising it needs nothing but a better score.
One known source of noise: 24 mutants are killed by timeout, and a slower or busier
machine could let some of those survive instead, costing about 1.3 points. If this
gate ever goes red without a test being removed, that is the first thing to check —
and the fix is to find out why those mutants are slow, not to move the number.
